Nomatic Travel Pack vs Aer Travel Pack 3 — Which Backpack Is Better for Digital Nomads?

Can't decide between the Nomatic Travel Pack and the Aer Travel Pack 3? We compare organization, durability, laptop protection, and comfort for remote workers who commute and travel.

5/27/2026by Jeff Vellingan700 words
digital-nomadcomparison
If your office is wherever you open your laptop, your backpack isn't just a bag — it's your mobile command center. The difference between a thoughtfully designed travel backpack and a random bag from the clearance rack is the difference between gliding through airport security and frantically unpacking your entire life to find a charging cable. Two bags that have earned cult followings among digital nomads are the Nomatic Travel Pack and the Aer Travel Pack 3. Both are purpose-built for people who carry tech, but they approach organization in very different ways. The Nomatic Travel Pack is the organizer's dream. It has over 20 pockets and compartments, and every single one feels intentional. The laptop compartment is padded and suspended off the bottom, so if you drop the bag, your laptop doesn't hit the ground. It fits up to a 16-inch laptop. There's a dedicated tablet sleeve, a RFID-safe pocket for your passport and cards, a magnetic water bottle pocket that lies flat when empty, and a ventilated shoe compartment at the bottom that doubles as a dirty laundry separator. The main compartment opens clamshell-style like a suitcase, which is brilliant for packing cubes or grabbing things without digging. The bag expands from 20L to 30L via a zipper, so it works as both a daily carry and a weekend trip bag. The material is water-resistant tarpaulin with YKK zippers. At around $250-280, it's an investment, but the organization genuinely changes how you travel. The main trade-off: the bag itself weighs about 4 pounds empty, which is on the heavier side. The Aer Travel Pack 3 takes a different philosophy — less compartment overload, more thoughtful simplicity. It holds 35L, which is the maximum most airlines allow as a carry-on. The laptop compartment is equally well-padded and fits up to a 16-inch device, plus it has a separate quick-access pocket at the top that lets you slide your laptop out at security without opening the main compartment. The Aer uses 1680D Cordura ballistic nylon, which is basically indestructible — this bag will outlast your career. The harness system deserves special mention: load lifters at the shoulders, a sternum strap, and a padded hip belt that tucks away when you don't need it. If you carry heavy loads or walk long distances through airports, the Aer's comfort is noticeably better than the Nomatic. The front admin panel is well-organized without being overwhelming, and the main compartment is a spacious bucket that works great with packing cubes. It's priced similarly at around $230-250. For daily commuting plus occasional short trips, the Nomatic Travel Pack wins on sheer organizational joy. Everything has a place, and that magnetic water bottle pocket is something you'll wonder how you lived without. For serious travelers who prioritize carrying comfort, durability, and maximum carry-on capacity, the Aer Travel Pack 3 is the better tool. Both will protect your tech, both look professional enough for client meetings, and both are a massive upgrade from stuffing your laptop into a gym bag. If you can, try both on with weight inside — the harness fit is very personal and can make or break your experience on a long travel day. --- **Products mentioned in this article:** - [Nomatic Travel Pack](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Nomatic+Travel+Pack+Backpack&tag=remotework-20) - [Aer Travel Pack 3](https://aer.com/collections/travel-bags/products/travel-pack-3) --- *Disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links.
